# harness-maker v0.28.9 — Cold Audit vs TECH_SPEC.md

## 1. Executive Summary

This is a healthy implementation wrapped in a stale specification. 77 confirmed findings were assessed after adversarial verification; the distribution is lopsided:

| Class | Count (approx) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| impl-correct / spec-stale (doc-only) | ~55 | Code is the deliberate, ADR-backed truth; spec/docs lag |
| spec-correct / impl-wrong (real defects) | ~11 | Genuine code/template/script bugs |
| both-wrong / neither-wrong / quality | ~8 | Internal contradictions, dead code, cosmetic |
| completeness-critic gaps still open | 3 | Not in confirmed set; 1 is high-severity |

**Alignment verdict.** The code faithfully implements the *current* design intent and is internally consistent (code + tests + CLAUDE.md + ADRs agree in almost every case). What is misaligned is the paper trail: TECH_SPEC.md is a ~v0.9–v0.12 era snapshot (still says "hold at 0.1.0", still lists `templates/` at repo root, still describes the 4-source crawl and `/hm:refresh` as live). README/PRIVACY/ARCHITECTURE were never swept after the two big deletions (ADR-0007 crawl removal in 0.22.3; the `/hm:ai-readiness`→`/hm:health` consolidation in 0.13.0).

**How much is just stale-spec.** The clear majority. None of these break installs or security. They matter because (a) README and rendered skill/dashboard files are *public and user-facing* and tell users to run commands that no longer exist (`/hm:refresh`, `/hm:ai-readiness`, `/hm:personalization-audit`), and (b) TECH_SPEC's acceptance checklist (`bash .claude-verify.sh all`) would have a human verifying retired behavior.

**Real defects.** The serious ones cluster in three places:
1. **Multi-document `harness.yaml` parse defect** (F27/F28 + the critic's spec_gate gap). The same `yaml.safe_load()` mistake recurs across three readers; the most damaging instance silently disables the spec-driven TDD gate.
2. **`verify-before-completion` SKILL drift** (F45/F46/F47/F48). Three of five checks are broken or no-op on modern installs; the SKILL applies a materially weaker gate than `/hm:verify`.
3. **Broken acceptance script** (F69/F71/F68/F70). The repo's documented verification entry point aborts in phase_1 at version 0.1.0.

**F27 — locale degradation.** `i18n.py:30` calls `yaml.safe_load(text)` on a file the renderer always prepends a `---` provenance block to (`render.py:909`). On a 2-document stream this raises `ComposerError` (a `YAMLError`), caught and swallowed → `DEFAULT_LOCALE`. Proven empirically: dogfood `harness.yaml` has `locale: ko` yet `resolve_locale()` returns `en` while `io_utils.load_harness_yaml()` returns `ko`. Every non-English user with a rendered harness gets English messages. CLAUDE.md §2 mandates `load_harness_yaml()` for exactly this reason. Fix: swap to the helper. Tests at `test_i18n.py:13` write bare bodies and mask the defect.

**F45 — health-delta gate is a no-op.** `SKILL.md.j2:59-66` reads `.claude/observability/metrics.jsonl` (the `_LEGACY_NAME`; modern telemetry writes dated `metrics-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`) and only sets a baseline `if 'health' in rec` — but no telemetry record ever carries a `health` key. So `metrics.exists()` is False → baseline=0 → `score >= -5` always True. The regression gate in the SKILL path never fires. The canonical stage (`stages/verify.md.j2:121-129`) already does this correctly via `dashboard.md` `## Structural`.

**F54 — P0 findings invisible to readiness.** `readiness.py:539` matches only `"severity": "high"`. But `hallucination.py:137` and `prod_name_guard.py:45,93` emit `P0`/`P1`/`P2`, never `high`. A persisted critical P0 (e.g. a hallucinated import, or Read→Write on a prod target) leaves `high_count=0` and the signal passes. `cli.py:1327` already gates on `{"high","P0"}`, proving P0 is meant to be critical. The vocabulary is unified everywhere except this one signal.

**F69 / F70 — broken acceptance gate.** `.claude-verify.sh` asserts `__version__ == '0.1.0'` (lines 94, 105) and aborts under `set -e` at 0.28.9, so `bash .claude-verify.sh all` — the documented verify entry point (TECH_SPEC.md:13, ARCHITECTURE.md:148) — never reaches a green run. Other phases require deleted templates (`dev.md`, `monitor.md`, `dashboard.{ko,en}.md.j2`). These are trivial script edits but high-severity because the project's own self-test is dead.

*Completeness-critic high-severity gap (not in confirmed set):* **`spec_gate.py:91`** `_load_yaml_keys()` has the identical bare `safe_load` defect. With `cfg={}` the gate's `dev_mode != 'spec-driven'` is always true → early `allow=True` → the spec-driven TDD PreToolUse enforcement is silently disabled on every real install. This is the third and worst instance of the F27/F28 family and should be treated as high. See §4.

Notable behavioral medium items needing scrutiny:

**F22 — false-positive personalization divergence.** `_load_preset_defaults` builds its baseline from a bare `InterviewAnswers(preset=preset)` (model-level defaults: `consensus='single'`, `default_workflow='exec-rev-wrap'`), but a real `/hm:make` Production install gets `consensus='cross-check'` and `default_workflow='exec-rev-ver-wrap'` via `_consensus_for`/`_default_for`. A Production user who *kept the defaults* is mis-classified as divergent — exactly the false positive PLAN-audit-convergence-2026-05 was built to eliminate. Fix is mechanical (seed the baseline via `_build_answers` + the `_*_for` helpers) but behavioral; add the two regression assertions.

**F35 — dashboard schema collision.** The seed template (`dashboard.md.j2`, last touched 0.4.0) renders an "AI Readiness Dashboard / ## Composite / ## Actions" body with a `<!-- @hm:user:extensions -->` block; the 0.22.3 runtime writer (`write_dashboard`) overwrites the same path with an incompatible "# Health / ## Structural / ## Personalization" body via plain `atomic_write` with no block-merge. Damage is bounded — the `/hm:health` slash command uses `--json-output` and bypasses `write_dashboard` — but a direct `harness-maker health .` silently destroys the user-extensions block.

**F30 / F50 — built-and-tested-but-dead machinery.** The recommendation registry (`recommend_all`, `_dispatch_recommendation`) and `cleanup_all()` are tested but never reached from production paths. F30 means the profiler's framework/CI/package-manager detection produces no user-visible effect beyond an audit echo; F50 means the documented "force cleanup on autoloop blocker" disk-accumulation defense can never fire. Both need a human decision: wire it up or explicitly mark dormant.

**F66 — banner never resets.** `sessionstart_drift.py` counts the entire append-only `overrides.jsonl` but the message says "since last audit"; once a project crosses 30 lifetime overrides the banner fires every session forever, even right after an audit. Fix: filter overrides to `ts > last_audit` (mirror L2 `_filter_recent`).

False — actual hooks wire only loop/permission/worktree/spec gates + telemetry; secscan runs on-demand via the security-scanner SKILL/agent, never by a hook. Misrepresents security posture in a rendered, always-on file. No confirmed finding touches this. |
| **cursor harness.mdc.j2 "five gates" count** (same file) | low | scan_all runs 7 gates; the .mdc says 5, omitting hallucination + prod_name_guard — the same two whose P0 findings F54 says readiness is blind to. Distinct rendered-file location from F57's Python-docstring finding. |

Recommend confirming the spec_gate gap with the same empirical reproduction used for F27 (write a provenance-prefixed `harness.yaml` with `dev_mode: spec-driven`, assert the gate blocks a test-write lacking a SPEC), then fixing all three parse sites in one pass with a shared helper.

7. **Parse-defect family — do together:** F27, F28, F29 (i18n + permission_gate + test) **and the critic's spec_gate gap.** Single shared `load_harness_yaml` adoption. Add provenance-prefixed regression fixtures so the masking never recurs.

10. **F45 / F46 / F47 / F48 — verify-before-completion SKILL.** Rewrite Check 3 (dashboard `## Structural` + no-baseline PASS), Check 2 (verification_cache + toolchain), Check 5 (branch-agnostic), and reconcile the SKILL with the canonical stage so the two gates can't drift. Snapshot regen required. Highest real-behavior value after the parse fixes. *Human gate: confirm the SKILL should mirror the stage rather than delegate to `/hm:verify`.*

14. **F35 — dashboard schema collision.** Update seed template to 0.22.3 schema and either drop the user-extensions block or teach `write_dashboard` to preserve it via block_merge. *Human gate: option (a) drop block vs (b) preserve.*

**Wave D — human decision required, do not auto-apply.**
15. **F30 — recommendation registry wiring.** Either wire `recommend_all`/`_dispatch_recommendation` into `interview()` (changes interactive UX; needs ordering decisions and autoloop-path handling) or explicitly mark dormant. Not safe to auto-apply.
16. **F50 — cleanup_all reachability.** Add `cleanup-all` subcommand + wire into autoloop blocker path, or remove the function and the CLAUDE.md claim. Behavioral; pick a direction first.
17. Cursor `.mdc` security-gate corrections (critic gaps): correct the false hook-wiring claim and the 5→7 gate count. Rendered ambient file — verify wording with the cross-IDE owner.

**Pure spec doc tasks (no code):** all of §3. Lowest urgency for runtime, but do the public README/PRIVACY/ARCHITECTURE items (Wave A.6) early since they are user-visible.
